problems.description: An edge is missing one of its two required geometric representations: either it has a 3D space curve but no 2D parametric curve (pcurve) on a face's host surface, or vice versa (a pcurve exists but no 3D curve). The healer synthesizes the missing representation by projecting the 3D curve onto the surface (or lifting the pcurve into 3D), skipping only the case where the host surface is a plane (pcurve is optional there). On periodic/closed surfaces, a seam edge additionally needs a second, period-shifted pcurve paired with the first.

problems.description: An edge carries a 3D curve or a pcurve whose endpoint(s), when evaluated, land farther from the edge's actual vertex position than the vertex tolerance allows (i.e., the curve representation itself is stale, wrong, or was computed for a different placement) — or a pcurve's declared parameter range does not correspond to a valid sub-domain of its curve (exceeds the curve's bounds or wraps past a periodic curve's period). Rather than trying to repair the curve in place, the healer discards the offending representation so it can be rebuilt fresh from the other (trusted) representation.

problems.description: An edge's endpoint vertex carries a tolerance value too small to actually contain the true geometric deviation between the vertex's 3D point and the edge curve's (or, when shared across multiple faces, several surfaces') endpoint evaluation. The vertex's tolerance ball does not reach the curve/surface geometry it is meant to index, so proximity and coincidence queries against it silently fail. The healer recomputes the required tolerance (accounting for all surfaces the vertex touches, not just one) and enlarges the vertex tolerance to cover the actual deviation.

problems.description: An edge's 3D curve and its pcurve(s) are not consistently parametrized ('not SameParameter'): evaluating both at the same parameter value produces points that diverge in 3D space by more than the edge's tolerance, even though the edge may be flagged as SameParameter=.T. in the input. The healer attempts to resynchronize the parametrizations (via BRepLib::SameParameter on a working copy), measures the resulting deviation against the original, picks whichever result has lower deviation, and raises the edge's (and its vertices') tolerance to bound the residual deviation.

problems.description: A single TopoDS_Vertex object is referenced by two different wires of the same face (e.g., an outer boundary wire and an inner/hole wire, or two hole wires) at a point where they touch. This is representable and tolerated inside OCCT's in-memory BRep model but is invalid for STEP export, where each wire must own distinct vertex instances even at coincident locations. The healer detects such cross-wire vertex sharing and splits the shared vertex into a fresh, independent copy for the second wire's edges, preserving position and tolerance.

problems.description: Two or more edges that are topologically connected (consecutive edges in a wire, or arbitrary edges registered as touching) reference geometrically coincident (within tolerance) but topologically DISTINCT vertex objects, instead of sharing one common vertex. The healer merges the group of coincident vertex instances into a single shared vertex, computing its position as the midpoint of the bounding box of all the original positions and its tolerance as the maximum deviation from that position (plus a small numerical margin), then rewires all affected edges to use the single merged vertex.

problems.description: Consecutive edges of a wire have endpoint vertices/curve-endpoints that do not merely duplicate-at-the-same-location (as in the previous problem) but genuinely disagree — there is an actual positional or parametric gap between where one edge's curve ends and the next edge's curve begins, exceeding trivial tolerance. problems.description: Two adjacent faces that physically touch along a common boundary each carry their own independent copy of the boundary edge (and its endpoint vertices) instead of referencing one shared topological edge — a geometric crack/gap in an otherwise visually-closed shell. The healer geometrically sews the registered face pairs together (via BRepBuilderAPI_Sewing), rebuilds the affected wires with the sewn/shared edges (reordering, re-fixing edge curves, and removing self-intersections introduced by the substitution), aggregates and repositions any resulting merged vertices (bounding-box-center position, inflated tolerance to cover all originals), and finally corrects face orientation after the wire reconstruction.

problems.description: A face is built directly on a fully closed/periodic surface (full cylinder, cone, torus, or sphere) without being explicitly split along the periodic seam, or is trimmed such that it still effectively wraps a full period in U and/or V. Many downstream consumers cannot represent or process a face that wraps a full period. The healer detects the seam — either from an explicit seam edge already present, or by testing whether the untrimmed surface is closed while the trimmed half is not — chooses to split along U or V based on which direction the seam's bounding box is anisotropic in, and recursively re-applies the split to results still closed in a remaining direction.

problems.description: Shape sub-elements (faces, edges, vertices, or entire branches of a compound) carry a non-identity TopLoc_Location transform applied at the topology level rather than having their geometry expressed directly in absolute/global coordinates. This is a normal and valid OCCT representation, but is inconvenient or actively broken for some consumers/algorithms/round-trips that don't correctly track or honor a placement stack, causing geometry to appear in the wrong place or stale-cached-location bugs during traversal. The healer rebuilds each affected surface, curve, and point by applying the transform directly to the geometry, then clears the location so the assembled shape carries no residual instance transforms.
